name: none
description: No opponent response: every player who was not moved keeps the observed position.
assumptions: Defenders do not react to the intervention.

name: marker_follows
description: Rule (legacy): the defender nearest to a relocated attacker's observed position (within 10 m) shifts by follow_fraction of the attacker's displacement.
assumptions: One marker per relocated attacker; no kinematic limit is applied (the move is still feasibility-checked like user moves).
This is not what the defender would have done; no ground truth exists for it.

Observational check (C37): with attackers' unexpected real movement as the intervention, this rule's moves match how real markers moved (about the right direction and size) on both providers, beyond a permuted placebo. Still a rule, not a prediction.
status: experimental: consistent with real defender reactions in an observational check on both providers (not a forecast, not an intervention validation)

name: press_carrier
description: Rule: when the carrier (with the ball) is relocated, the nearest outfield defender closes toward the new carrier position, stopping 1.5 m short, as far as the kinematic envelope allows.
assumptions: Only one defender presses; teammates do not cover the space it leaves.
Differential response: a defender moves by the change in the policy's target position caused by the intervention, so an unchanged situation produces no move.

Each move is limited to the defender's kinematic envelope over the horizon (envelope v2: no reaction delay, <= 7.0 m/s^2 braking or turning, speeding up <= 7(1 - v/9) m/s^2, <= 9.0 m/s, 0.10 s velocity lag) from the observed position and causal velocity. A reachable move is not a tactically plausible one.

Only outfield defenders are moved; attackers, goalkeepers and user-moved players never are. Moves respect the pitch bounds and a 0.5 m separation (resolved by shortening the move, in player-id order).
This is not what the defender would have done; no ground truth exists for it.

Observational check (C37): not supported with the current envelope (v2): its moves are larger than real pressing reactions (real movement is 0.3-0.6 of them) and worse than constant velocity on SkillCorner. Under the tighter session-3 envelope it was consistent with real pressing on Metrica only. Treat its moves as an illustration of the assumption.
status: experimental: not supported by the observational check under the current kinematic envelope

name: zonal_shift
description: Rule: the outfield defenders shift 50% of the ball's lateral and 30% of its longitudinal displacement on top of their current motion, each clipped to its kinematic envelope.
assumptions: The shift fractions are a priori assumptions, not fitted to data.
Triggered only when the ball moves (i.e. the carrier is relocated).
Differential response: a defender moves by the change in the policy's target position caused by the intervention, so an unchanged situation produces no move.

Each move is limited to the defender's kinematic envelope over the horizon (envelope v2: no reaction delay, <= 7.0 m/s^2 braking or turning, speeding up <= 7(1 - v/9) m/s^2, <= 9.0 m/s, 0.10 s velocity lag) from the observed position and causal velocity. A reachable move is not a tactically plausible one.

Only outfield defenders are moved; attackers, goalkeepers and user-moved players never are. Moves respect the pitch bounds and a 0.5 m separation (resolved by shortening the move, in player-id order).
This is not what the defender would have done; no ground truth exists for it.

Observational check (C37): real defensive blocks shift much less than this rule assumes (real movement is 0.13-0.22 of its simulated moves), on both providers. Treat its moves as an illustration of the assumption, not as a plausible response.
status: experimental: overshoots real defensive movement in the observational check

name: lane_cover
description: Rule: when a non-carrier attacker is relocated, the outfield defender who can get closest to the new carrier-to-attacker passing lane moves toward the nearest point of that lane, clipped to its kinematic envelope.
assumptions: One defender per relocated attacker, chosen by reachability of the lane.
The lane is a straight segment to the attacker's position (no lead pass).
Differential response: a defender moves by the change in the policy's target position caused by the intervention, so an unchanged situation produces no move.

Each move is limited to the defender's kinematic envelope over the horizon (envelope v2: no reaction delay, <= 7.0 m/s^2 braking or turning, speeding up <= 7(1 - v/9) m/s^2, <= 9.0 m/s, 0.10 s velocity lag) from the observed position and causal velocity. A reachable move is not a tactically plausible one.

Only outfield defenders are moved; attackers, goalkeepers and user-moved players never are. Moves respect the pitch bounds and a 0.5 m separation (resolved by shortening the move, in player-id order).
This is not what the defender would have done; no ground truth exists for it.

Observational check (C37): with attackers' unexpected real movement as the intervention, this rule's moves match real defender movement in direction on both providers, beyond a permuted placebo; with the current envelope (v2) real defenders move about 0.8 of its simulated moves. Still a rule, not a prediction.
status: experimental: consistent with real defender reactions in an observational check on both providers (not a forecast, not an intervention validation)

name: learned
description: Forecaster, not an intervention model: a ridge model of short-horizon defender displacement fit on real tracking (per provider, leave-one-match-out evaluated), applied to every outfield defender as the difference between its forecast for the hypothetical and the observed state, clipped to the kinematic envelope.
assumptions: The model forecasts how defenders moved in real play (observational). Its validation does not cover responses to hypothetical interventions.

Why it barely reacts: an intervention changes only its position-offset inputs, and in real play those offsets explain almost none of how defenders deviate from their own motion (about 1 cm per metre; session-4 diagnostics). The intervened inputs are not out of distribution: the model is accurate about the evolution of play and uninformative about reactions.
Forecast horizon is capped at the longest trained horizon (1.0 s).

The fitted model is dominated by the defender's own velocity (close to damped constant velocity), so its responses to interventions are very small (centimetres; docs/RESEARCH.md). Validated forecasting does not make it a strong response model.
Linear in causal features: own velocity, ball offset and velocity, nearest-attacker offset, own-goal offset.
Differential response: a defender moves by the change in the policy's target position caused by the intervention, so an unchanged situation produces no move.

Each move is limited to the defender's kinematic envelope over the horizon (envelope v2: no reaction delay, <= 7.0 m/s^2 braking or turning, speeding up <= 7(1 - v/9) m/s^2, <= 9.0 m/s, 0.10 s velocity lag) from the observed position and causal velocity. A reachable move is not a tactically plausible one.

Only outfield defenders are moved; attackers, goalkeepers and user-moved players never are. Moves respect the pitch bounds and a 0.5 m separation (resolved by shortening the move, in player-id order).
This is not what the defender would have done; no ground truth exists for it.
status: validated: short-horizon forecasts of real play beat constant velocity

name: learned_innovation
description: Ridge model of how defenders deviate from their own constant velocity when attackers (and the ball) deviate from theirs, fit on real tracking per provider and leave-one-match-out evaluated. A relocation is treated as the relocated attacker's unexpected movement over the horizon (and the ball's, when the carrier moves); each outfield defender moves by the predicted change, clipped to its kinematic envelope.
assumptions: Observational association, not a causal effect: attackers and defenders share drivers in real play. A permuted-innovation placebo isolates the part specific to the attacker-defender geometry; the served status says whether the pre-registered rule was met for this provider.
Response weights depend on distance at the analysed frame: nearest attacker, attackers within about 5 m and 15 m, and the attacking team as a whole.
Linear: a relocation larger than real unexpected movement (99% of attacker innovations are below about 2.3 m (Metrica) / 2.5 m (SkillCorner) in 1 s; exact values in fitted_range) is an extrapolation.
Forecast horizon is capped at the longest trained horizon (1.0 s).
Differential response: a defender moves by the change in the policy's target position caused by the intervention, so an unchanged situation produces no move.

Each move is limited to the defender's kinematic envelope over the horizon (envelope v2: no reaction delay, <= 7.0 m/s^2 braking or turning, speeding up <= 7(1 - v/9) m/s^2, <= 9.0 m/s, 0.10 s velocity lag) from the observed position and causal velocity. A reachable move is not a tactically plausible one.

Only outfield defenders are moved; attackers, goalkeepers and user-moved players never are. Moves respect the pitch bounds and a 0.5 m separation (resolved by shortening the move, in player-id order).
This is not what the defender would have done; no ground truth exists for it.
status: validated (observational): given attackers' real unexpected movement, its defender forecasts beat constant velocity and a permuted placebo

fitted_range.quantity: off-ball attacker innovation (displacement beyond own constant velocity)
